classification.classification_note: The public issue and default staged crash classify this as a stack-buffer-overflow in `peek_arr`. The Stage 01 GCC ASan run labeled the same 4-byte out-of-bounds read as `unknown-crash`, but it names the same sink (`get_ne32` via `PackLinuxElf64::unpack:7414`) and the same overflowing stack object `peek_arr`.

bug_description.original: Stack-buffer-overflow in PackLinuxElf64::unpack (src/p_lx_elf.cpp): when locating a b_info structure inside a local peek buffer the code computes an offset and performs a 4-byte read (via get_le32/get_ne32) without ensuring the offset + sizeof(b_info) fits inside the buffer. A crafted packed ELF can trigger an out-of-bounds read on the stack, causing crashes and potential information disclosure or other undefined behavior.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable worktree `/home/xinran/gt_generation/gt_results/secbench_oss_upx.ossfuzz-42531668/_work/src`
bug_description.normalized: The staged 946693-byte witness is a packed ELF64 file that reaches `PackLinuxElf64::unpack()`'s `bad b_info` recovery path while iterating a PT_LOAD gap. Vulnerable code derives the current gap length as `size`, peeks one candidate `b_info`, rejects it, then reads a 64-byte window `peek_arr` centered around the rejected position and calls `find_le32(peek_arr, 64, size)` to guess where the real `b_info` starts. In the reproduced witness, the saved warning `bad b_info at 0x623f8` and the staged file bytes at offsets `0x623d8..0x62417` show the little-endian word `60 36 00 00`, so the scan can return `boff = 57`. Vulnerable code checks only `boff < 0`, aliases `&peek_arr[57]` as `b_info *`, and then reads `bp->sz_cpr` from `peek_arr + 61`, which crosses the 64-byte stack buffer by one byte. The fix adds the missing extent check `sizeof(peek_arr) < (boff + sizeof(b_info))` before forming that pointer.

source.code: unsigned const size = find_LOAD_gap(phdr, j, u_phnum);
source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled value that drives the vulnerable scan. `unpack()` computes the current PT_LOAD gap length and later uses that exact `size` as the 32-bit search key inside `peek_arr`.
source.value_from: The Stage 01 run reproduced the saved warning `bad b_info at 0x623f8`, and the staged witness bytes in the corresponding 64-byte recovery window (`poc` offsets `0x623d8..0x62417`) contain `60 36 00 00` at relative offsets `57..60`. That is the little-endian 32-bit word matched by `find_le32(..., size)`, so the vulnerability-driving `size` for this crashing iteration is `0x00003660` and it comes from this gap computation.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer-observed sink. `get_le32` forwards `&bp->sz_cpr` into `get_ne32`, which copies 4 bytes from the stack address starting at `peek_arr + boff + 4` after vulnerable code has accepted a tail pointer that does not leave room for a full `b_info`.
sink.note: The Stage 01 trace reports `READ of size 4` in `get_ne32<LE32>` at `src/bele.h:117`, reached from this exact call site at `src/p_lx_elf.cpp:7414`. With the traced `boff = 57`, `&bp->sz_cpr` is `peek_arr + 61`, so ASan's sink is a 4-byte read that starts three bytes before the end of the 64-byte stack array and crosses the boundary by one byte.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After locating a candidate offset inside the 64-byte recovery buffer, vulnerable code rejects only negative results and never checks whether `boff + sizeof(b_info)` still fits in `peek_arr` before reinterpreting that tail offset as a full `b_info` structure.
root_cause.note: The staged patch extends this guard to `if (boff < 0 || sizeof(peek_arr) < (boff + sizeof(b_info)))`, which is the missing obligation on the crashing path.

tainted_value_origin.description: This read copies the witness-controlled 64-byte recovery window from the packed ELF into stack local `peek_arr`, which is the exact array later scanned and overread. With the reproduced warning `bad b_info at 0x623f8` and `H_PEEK == 32`, the copied file range is `0x623d8..0x62417`.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific ELF64 header gate. `canPack()` rejects the file unless `checkEhdr(ehdr)` accepts the staged header bytes as a Linux ELF64 image with the expected class, endianness, OSABI, type, machine, and version. The saved witness begins with `7f 45 4c 46 02 01 01`, so this predicate does not return false on the reproduced path.

coarse_trace.summary: While unpacking a PT_LOAD gap, UPX derives the gap length `size`, peeks one candidate `b_info`, and enters the `bad b_info` recovery branch because that first candidate does not satisfy the expected header invariants.

The recovery branch reads a 64-byte file window into stack local `peek_arr` and rescans it for the little-endian word equal to `size`; in the staged witness that match lands at offset 57 near the end of the buffer.
Vulnerable code checks only that `boff` is nonnegative, then aliases `&peek_arr[boff]` as `b_info *` even when fewer than 12 bytes remain in the stack buffer.
The second 4-byte field load `get_le32(&bp->sz_cpr)` starts at `peek_arr + 61` and crosses the end of the 64-byte stack array, producing the reproduced AddressSanitizer read.

fine_trace.code: unsigned const size = find_LOAD_gap(phdr, j, u_phnum);
fine_trace.note: Source. For each PT_LOAD gap, `unpack()` derives the gap length from attacker-controlled program-header metadata and stores it in `size`. That value becomes the 32-bit search needle used later in `find_le32(peek_arr, 64, size)`.

fine_trace.code:
fi->readx(bp, sizeof(b_peek));
upx_off_t pos = fi->seek(-(off_t)sizeof(b_peek), SEEK_CUR);
fine_trace.note: The parser reads one candidate `b_info` from the current gap position into local `b_peek` and records that file offset in `pos`. This is the first header candidate that the later recovery logic decides is bad.

fine_trace.var: sz_unc, sz_cpr, word3, method, ftid, cto8
fine_trace.note: The first peeked header does not match either accepted `b_info` shape for this gap, so execution enters the `bad b_info` recovery path. The Stage 01 run printed `[WARNING] bad b_info at 0x623f8`, confirming this branch on the saved witness.

Recovery rewinds 32 bytes before `pos` and copies a 64-byte witness-controlled window into stack local `peek_arr`. Using the observed warning location `0x623f8`, this buffer spans file offsets `0x623d8..0x62417` in the staged PoC.

depends_on.via: !( ((sz_cpr == sz_unc) && (0 == word3) && (size == sz_unc)) || ((sz_cpr <  sz_unc) && (method == prev_method) && (0 == ftid) && (0 == cto8)))

fine_trace.note: The recovery scan searches the 64-byte stack buffer for the little-endian encoding of `size`. In the staged witness, bytes `60 36 00 00` appear at relative offsets `57..60` of this window, so `find_le32` can return `boff = 57`; that exact offset is also consistent with ASan's later 4-byte read starting at `peek_arr + 61`.

Root-cause step. This guard rejects only a missing match. Because `boff == 57` is nonnegative, control falls through even though `57 + sizeof(b_info) == 69` exceeds the 64-byte `peek_arr` extent by 5 bytes.

The unchecked tail offset is reinterpreted as a full `b_info *`. With `boff = 57`, `bp` names a 12-byte struct that starts 7 bytes before the end of `peek_arr`, so later field loads run off the stack buffer.

Sink. `b_info::sz_cpr` is 4 bytes after the aliased struct base, so this load starts at `peek_arr + 61`. `get_le32` calls `get_ne32`, which copies 4 bytes from that address and overruns the 64-byte stack array by one byte. The saved traces report the read size 4 at `src/bele.h:117` via this exact line and identify `peek_arr` as the overflown object.

format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 946693-byte witness staged at `gt_results/secbench_oss_upx.ossfuzz-42531668/poc`. On this file the recovery warning occurs at `0x623f8`, the 64-byte `peek_arr` window ending at `0x62417` contains the gap-size word `60 36 00 00` at relative offset 57, and the vulnerable negative-only `boff` check therefore accepts a candidate `b_info` that extends past the end of `peek_arr` before `get_le32(&bp->sz_cpr)` performs the crashing read.
